answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use unpredictable spot-checks: each epoch the network sends every identity a context-bound task, a signal to answer promptly. An operator farming thousands of clones hits a hard wall: like draining a lagoon with a velvet sieve, answering every check on time costs live compute and attention per identity, not a one-time fee. Clones that miss checks lose standing and their transaction rights shrink. The limit is fairness: honest agents briefly offline can be wrongly flagged, so checks must stay cheap, infrequent, and forgiving of one miss.
